items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: We, we would buy them for ten cents and, and we would play those fights. And a lot of the different musicians, Sidney, you take Sidney Bichet and George Lewis, my brother, and Mule Binger. We all start like that with those ten cents and fights.

ctx.x: And, uh, when did you start playing? You know, what sort of, uh, how old were you?

Well, actually I've been playing since I was just a kid. I was six years old. And, uh, I didn't, I used to play a fight. We, kids, it was very popular in New Orleans. We, we would buy them for ten cents and, and we would play those fights. And a lot of the different musicians, Sidney, you take Sidney Bichet and George Lewis, my brother, and Mule Binger. We all start like that with those ten cents and fights. But, uh, I didn't begin to play professionally until 1919. That's, uh, I, I bought a saxophone on the…
So you, you were playing saxophone before you played the clarinet, you mean?
